chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so a man came to him and asked him about a man who married a woman, and she died before he had consummated the marriage with her: 'Can he marry her mother?' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from us has done it, and we did not see any problem with that.'

So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Shia do not pride themselves except with the judgment of Ali (peace be upon him) regarding this 'Shamkhiyya' case, about which Ibn Mas'ud had issued a fatwa that there is no problem with that. Then he went to Ali (peace be upon him) and asked him, so Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'From where did you take it?'
And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame on you

He said, 'From the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: And your step-daughters who are in your guardianship, (born) of your wives to whom you have gone in, but if you have not gone in to them, there is no blame on you.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'This is an exclusion, and this is for copulation, and mothers of your wives.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to the man: 'Did you hear what this one is reporting from Ali (peace be upon him)?' So when I stood up, I was remorseful, and I said (to myself): 'What have I done? He (peace be upon him) was saying, 'A man from us has done it, and we did not see any problem with that', and I was saying, 'Ali (peace be upon him) has judged with regards to it.'

So I met him (peace be upon him) after that, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The question of the man, that which I had said was a slip from me, so what are you saying with regards to it?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Sheikh! You inform me that Ali (peace be upon him) has judged with it, and you are asking me what I am saying with regards to it?'

key_terms.الشَّمْخِيَّةِ: A specific case or precedent regarding marriage rulings
key_terms.دَخَلُوا بِهِنَّ: Consummation of marriage (literally: entering with them)
key_terms.مُرْسَلَةٌ: Dispatched/General (referring to the general rule of mothers)
key_terms.مُسْتَثْنَاةٌ: Excluded (referring to the condition of consummation)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his wife's mother if she dies before he consummates the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential nuance between the Imams' practical acceptance of marrying a wife's mother (based on a companion's precedent) and the stricter textual argument attributed to Ali (AS) regarding Quran 4:23. The narrator’s self-reproach underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on aligning legal rulings with the precise linguistic distinctions in the Quranic verse, specifically distinguishing between step-daughters (where consummation matters) and mothers (who are perpetually prohibited).
